a possible mechanism of action of corticosteroids, namely the inhibition of the IL 2 binding to IL-2 receptors.
the mechanisms by which corticosteroids inhibit IL-2 induced T-lymphocyte proliferation.

HC interferes at the level of the IL-3 receptor, but not with the binding of IL2 to the IL-2-receptor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HC interferes in the interaction between IL-2 and its receptor.
HC inhibits IL-2 binding to IL-2 receptors by a mechanism other than the binding to the ligand itself.
IL-2 is a potent inducer of lymphocyte proliferation, but its action is counteracted by the presence of corticosteroids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corticosteroids inhibit the IL-2 response by interfering with IL-2 binding and/or signal transduction.
IL-2 binding is not a good indicator of biological activity of IL-2.
corticosteroids are not just immunosuppressive but also immunomodulating agents.
